    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="auditor_report">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING
FIRM</a></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To the
Board of Directors and Stockholders of Nicor Inc.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have
audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets and statements of
capitalization of Nicor Inc. and subsidiaries (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) as of December 31,
2009 and 2008, and the related consolidated statements of operations, common
equity, comprehensive income and cash flows for each of the three years in the
period ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Our audits also included the
financial statement schedule at Item 15(a)(2).&#160;&#160;We also have audited
the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2009,
based on criteria established in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Internal Control &#8212; Integrated
Framework </font>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the
Treadway Commission.&#160;&#160;The Company's management is responsible for
these financial statements and financial statement schedule, for maintaining
effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of
the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the
accompanying Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial
Reporting.&#160;&#160;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these
financial statements and financial statement schedule and an opinion on the
Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our
audits.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company
Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160;&#160;Those standards require
that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether
the financial statements are free of material misstatement and whether effective
internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material
respects.&#160;&#160;Our audits of the financial statements included examining,
on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the
financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant
estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement
presentation.&#160;&#160;Our audit of internal control over financial reporting
included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial
reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and
evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on
the assessed risk.&#160;&#160;Our audits also included performing such other
procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&#160;&#160;We
believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our
opinions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or
under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal
financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the
company's board of directors, management, and other personnel to provide
reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the
preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with
generally accepted accounting principles.&#160;&#160;A company's internal
control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)
pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and
fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company;
(2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to
permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted
accounting principles and that receipts and expenditures of the company are
being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of
the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely
detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's
assets that could have a material effect on the financial
statements.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Because
of the inherent limitations of internal control over financial reporting,
including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of
controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may not be prevented or
detected on a timely basis.&#160;&#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of
the effectiveness of the internal control over financial reporting to future
periods are subject to the risk that the controls may become inadequate because
of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or
procedures may deteriorate.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;ACCOUNTING
POLICIES</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Consolidation.</font>&#160;&#160;The
consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Nicor and all
majority-owned subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Nicor&#8217;s key subsidiaries are described
in Note 15 &#8211; Business Segment and Geographic Information.&#160;&#160;All
significant intercompany balances and transactions have been
eliminated.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of
estimates.</font>&#160;&#160;The preparation of the financial statements in
conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States
requires management to make estimates that affect reported
amounts.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates and such
differences could be material.&#160;&#160;Accounting estimates requiring
significant management judgment involve accrued unbilled revenues, derivative
instruments, regulatory assets and liabilities, pension and other postretirement
benefits, potential asset impairments, asset retirement obligations, loss
contingencies including environmental contingencies, credit risk and income
taxes.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Subsequent
events.&#160;&#160;</font>The company&#8217;s management evaluated subsequent events
for potential recognition and disclosure through February 24, 2010, the date
these financial statements were issued.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash and cash
equivalents.</font>&#160;&#160;Cash equivalents are comprised of highly liquid
investments of domestic subsidiaries with an initial maturity of three months or
less.&#160;&#160;The carrying value of these investments approximates fair
value.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory assets and
liabilities.</font>&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas is regulated by the ICC, which
establishes the rules and regulations governing utility rates and services in
Illinois.&#160;&#160;As a rate-regulated company, Nicor Gas is required to
recognize the economic effects of rate regulation and, accordingly, has recorded
regulatory assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Regulatory assets represent
probable future revenue associated with certain costs that are expected to be
recovered from customers through rate riders or base rates, upon approval by the
ICC.&#160;&#160;Regulatory liabilities represent probable future reductions in
revenues collected from ratepayers through a rate rider or base rates, or
probable future expenditures.&#160;&#160;If Nicor Gas&#8217; operations become no
longer subject to rate regulation, a write-off of net regulatory liabilities
would be required.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">All items

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ICC
does not presently allow Nicor Gas the opportunity to earn a return on its
regulatory postretirement asset.&#160;&#160;The regulatory postretirement asset
is expected to be recovered from ratepayers over a period of approximately 10 to
12 years.&#160;&#160;The regulatory assets related to debt are not included in
rate base, but are recovered over the term of the debt through the rate of
return authorized by the ICC.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas is allowed to recover and is
required to pay, using short-term interest rates, the carrying costs related to
temporary under or overcollections of natural gas costs and certain
environmental costs charged to its customers.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investments.&#160;&#160;</font>The
company&#8217;s investments in marketable securities are categorized at the date of
acquisition as trading, held-to-maturity, or
available-for-sale.&#160;&#160;Trading securities, which include money market
funds, are carried at fair value and are classified as current assets unless
held to satisfy a long-term obligation.&#160;&#160;The company classifies money
market funds held by its non-U.S. subsidiaries as short-term investments and all
others are classified as cash equivalents.&#160;&#160;Securities are categorized
as held-to-maturity when the company has the&#160;date positive intent and
ability to hold the securities to maturity.&#160;&#160;Held-to-maturity
securities are included in either short-term or long-term investments based upon
their contractual maturity date.&#160;&#160;The company carries held-to-maturity
securities at amortized cost, which approximates fair
value.&#160;&#160;Available-for-sale securities are carried at fair value, with
unrealized gains and losses, net of tax, reported in common equity as a
component of accumulated other comprehensive
income.&#160;&#160;Available-for-sale securities are classified as noncurrent
assets unless the intent is to sell the security within 12
months.&#160;&#160;The specific identification method is used to determine
realized gains or losses on the sale of marketable securities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Equity
investments.</font>&#160;&#160;The company invests in partnerships and limited
liability companies that are accounted for under the equity
method.&#160;&#160;Related investment balances classified as long-term
investments at December 31, 2009 and 2008 were $99.6 million and $107.5 million,
respectively, and include $84.8 million and $88.0 million at December 31, 2009
and 2008, respectively, related to Triton.</font></div>

        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents </a></font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Goodwill.</font>&#160;&#160;Goodwill
is the excess cost of an acquired business over the fair value of assets
acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination.&#160;&#160;Tropical
Shipping had goodwill of $20.9 million and $19.0 million at December 31, 2009
and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;The increase in goodwill from December 31,
2008 to December 31, 2009 is due primarily to an acquisition in the fourth
quarter of 2009.&#160;&#160;Nicor Services had goodwill of $4.0 million at both
December 31, 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;Goodwill is classified in noncurrent
other assets and is tested for impairment annually.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Asset retirement
obligations.</font>&#160;&#160;The company records legal obligations associated
with the retirement of long-lived assets in the period in which the obligation
is incurred, if sufficient information exists to reasonably estimate the fair
value of the obligation.&#160;&#160;When an asset retirement obligation is
recorded as a liability, a corresponding amount is recorded as an asset
retirement cost (an additional cost of the long-lived
asset).&#160;&#160;Subsequently, the asset retirement obligation is accreted to
the expected settlement amount and the asset retirement cost is depreciated over
the life of the asset on a straight-line basis.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Subject
to rate regulation, Nicor Gas continues to accrue all future asset retirement
costs through depreciation over the lives of its assets even when a legal
retirement obligation does not exist or insufficient information exists to
determine the fair value of the obligation.&#160;&#160;Amounts charged to
depreciation by Nicor Gas for future retirement costs, in excess of the normal
depreciation and accretion described above, are classified as a regulatory asset
retirement liability.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Derivative
instruments.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;
</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash flows from derivative
instruments are recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, and
gains and losses are recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Operations, in
the same categories as the underlying transactions.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash flow
hedge accounting may be elected only for highly effective hedges, based upon an
assessment, performed at least quarterly, of the historical and probable future
correlation of cash flows from the derivative instrument to changes in the
expected future cash flows of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;To the extent cash
flow hedge accounting is applied, the effective portion of any changes in the
fair value of the derivative instruments is reported as a component of
accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;Ineffectiveness, if any, is
immediately recognized in operating income.&#160;&#160;The amount in accumulated
other comprehensive income is reclassified to earnings when the forecasted
transaction is recognized in the Consolidated Statement of Operations, even if
the derivative instrument is sold, extinguished or terminated prior to the
transaction occurring.&#160;&#160;If the forecasted transaction is no longer
expected to occur, the amount in accumulated other comprehensive income is
immediately reclassified to operating income.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Nicor
Gas</font>.&#160;&#160;Derivative instruments, such as futures contracts,
options and swap agreements, are utilized primarily in the purchase of natural
gas for customers.&#160;&#160;These derivative instruments are reflected at fair
value.&#160;&#160;Realized gains or losses on such instruments are included in
the cost of gas delivered and are passed directly through to customers, subject
to ICC review, and therefore have no direct impact on
earnings.&#160;&#160;Unrealized changes in the fair value of these derivative
instruments are deferred as regulatory assets or liabilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At times,
Nicor Gas enters into futures contracts, options, swap agreements and
fixed-price purchase agreements to reduce the earnings volatility of certain
forecasted operating costs arising from fluctuations in natural gas prices, such
as the purchase of natural gas for use in company operations.&#160;&#160;These
derivative instruments are carried at fair value, unless they qualify for the
normal purchases and normal sales exception, in which case they are carried at
cost.&#160;&#160;To the extent hedge accounting is not elected, changes in such
fair values are immediately recorded in the current period as operating and
maintenance expense.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Nicor
Enerchange</font>.&#160;&#160;Derivative instruments, such as futures contracts,
options, forward contracts, swap agreements and other energy-related contracts
are held by Nicor&#8217;s wholesale natural gas marketing business, Nicor Enerchange,
for trading purposes.&#160;&#160;Certain of these derivative instruments are
used to economically hedge price risk associated with inventories of natural
gas, fixed-price purchase and sale agreements and other future natural gas
commitments.&#160;&#160;Nicor Enerchange records such derivative</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">50</div>

      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents </a></font></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">instruments
at fair value and generally cannot elect hedge accounting.&#160;&#160;As a
result, changes in derivative fair values may have a material impact on Nicor&#8217;s
financial statements.&#160;&#160;Other derivative instruments are used by Nicor
Enerchange to hedge price risks related to certain utility-bill management
products.&#160;&#160;These derivative instruments are carried at fair value and
cash flow hedge accounting may or may not be elected.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Nicor.</font>&#160;&#160;For
derivative instruments that were designated as hedges of interest payments on
30-year bonds issued by Nicor Gas in December 2003, the amount of loss deferred
at settlement in accumulated other comprehensive income is being amortized to
interest expense on a straight-line basis over the remaining life of the
bonds.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Credit risk and
concentrations.</font>&#160;&#160;Nicor&#8217;s major subsidiaries have diversified
customer bases and the company believes that it maintains prudent credit
policies which mitigate customer receivable, supplier performance and derivative
counterparty credit risk<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.&#160;&#160;</font>The company is
exposed to credit risk in the event a customer or supplier defaults on a
contract to pay for or deliver product at agreed-upon terms and conditions, or a
counterparty to a derivative instrument defaults on a settlement or otherwise
fails to perform under contractual terms.&#160;&#160;To manage this risk, the
company has established procedures to determine and monitor the creditworthiness
of counterparties, to seek guarantees or collateral back-up in the form of cash
or letters of credit, to acquire credit insurance in certain instances, and to
limit its exposure to any one counterparty.&#160;&#160;Nicor also, in some
instances, enters into netting arrangements to mitigate counterparty credit
risk.&#160;&#160;Credit losses are accrued when probable and reasonably
estimable.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
February 2, 2010, the ICC approved a bad debt rider that was filed for in 2009
by Nicor Gas.&#160;&#160;The bad debt rider provides for the recovery from (or
refund to) customers of the difference between the actual bad debt expense Nicor
Gas incurs on an annual basis and the benchmark bad debt expense included in its
rates for the respective year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenue
recognition.</font>&#160;&#160;Gas distribution revenues are recognized when
natural gas is delivered to customers.&#160;&#160;In accordance with ICC
regulations and subject to its review, the cost of gas delivered is charged to
customers without markup, although the timing of cost recovery can
vary.&#160;&#160;Temporary under and overcollections of gas costs are deferred
or accrued as a regulatory asset or liability with a corresponding decrease or
increase to cost of gas, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor Gas
accrues revenues for estimated deliveries to customers from the date of their
last bill until the balance sheet date.&#160;&#160;Receivables include accrued
unbilled revenues of $141.0 million and $199.1 million at December 31, 2009 and
2008, respectively, related primarily to gas distribution
operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor Gas
classifies revenue taxes billed to customers as operating revenues and related
taxes incurred as operating expenses.&#160;&#160;Revenue taxes included in
operating expense for 2009, 2008 and 2007 were $148.1 million, $171.1 million
and $148.7 million, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the
shipping business, revenues and related delivery costs are recognized at the
time vessels depart from port.&#160;&#160;While alternative methods of
recognizing shipping revenue and related costs exist, the difference between
those methods and the company&#8217;s policy does not have a material impact on
operating results.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor
Enerchange presents revenue from natural gas sales, cost of sales, and related
derivative instruments, which are entered into for trading purposes, on a net
basis.&#160;&#160;For Nicor Solutions and Nicor Advanced Energy, revenue is
recognized on their 12-month utility-bill management contracts as the lesser of
cumulative earned or cumulative billed amounts.&#160;&#160;Nicor Services
recognizes revenue for warranty and repair contracts on a straight-line basis
over the contract term.&#160;&#160;Revenue for maintenance services is
recognized at the time such services are performed.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>

        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents </a></font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Repair and maintenance
expense.</font>&#160;&#160;Nicor records expense for repair and maintenance
costs as incurred.&#160;&#160;The shipping business uses the direct expensing
method for planned major maintenance related to dry-docking and major repairs of
its owned vessels.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Legal defense
costs.</font>&#160;&#160;The company accrues estimated legal defense costs
associated with loss contingencies in the period in which it determines that
such costs are probable of being incurred and are reasonably
estimable.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Depreciation.</font>&#160;&#160;Property,
plant and equipment are depreciated over estimated useful lives on a
straight-line basis.&#160;&#160;The gas distribution business composite
depreciation rate is 4.1 percent, which includes all estimated future retirement
costs.&#160;&#160;Upon the retirement of these assets, no gain or loss is
recognized.&#160;&#160;In the shipping business, the estimated useful lives of
vessels range from 20 to 25 years.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income
taxes.&#160;&#160;</font>Deferred income taxes are provided at the current
statutory income tax rate for temporary differences between the tax basis
(adjusted for related unrecognized tax benefits, if any) of an asset or
liability and its reported amount in the financial statements.&#160;&#160;In the
gas distribution business, investment tax credits and regulatory income tax
liabilities for deferred taxes in excess of the current statutory rate are
amortized to income over the lives of the related properties.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
deferred income tax liability is not recorded on undistributed foreign earnings
that are expected in management&#8217;s judgment to be indefinitely reinvested
offshore.&#160;&#160;Management considers, among other factors, actual cash
investments offshore as well as projected cash requirements in making this
determination.&#160;&#160;Changes in management&#8217;s investment or repatriation
plans or circumstances could result in a different deferred income tax
liability.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
company records unrecognized tax benefits based on a recognition threshold and
valuation method to recognize and measure an income tax position taken, or
expected to be taken, in a tax return.&#160;&#160;The evaluation is based on a
two-step approach.&#160;&#160;The first step requires the company to evaluate
whether the tax position would &#8220;more likely than not,&#8221; based upon its technical
merits, be sustained upon examination by the appropriate taxing
authority.&#160;&#160;The second step requires the tax position to be measured
at the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50 percent likely of
being realized upon settlement.&#160;&#160;The company recognizes accrued
interest related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense and interest
income.&#160;&#160;Penalties, if any, are recorded in operating
expense.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;NEW
ACCOUNTING PRONOUNCEMENT</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair value measurements.</font>&#160;
Effective January 1, 2008, the company adopted the new requirements for fair
value measurements and disclosures.&#160;&#160;These requirements define fair
value, establish a consistent framework for measuring fair value and expand
disclosure requirements about fair value.&#160;&#160;These new requirements do
not establish any new fair value measurements, but rather provide guidance on
how to perform fair value measurements as required or permitted under other
accounting standards.&#160;&#160;They also provide for immediate recognition of
trade-date gains and losses related to certain derivative transactions whose
fair value has been determined using unobservable market
inputs.&#160;&#160;Nicor elected the one-year deferral allowed by the new
requirements<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>for
certain nonfinancial assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;As it applies to Nicor,
the deferral pertains to fair value measurements for business combinations,
asset retirement obligations and impairment testing of goodwill and other
intangible assets.&#160;&#160;The effect of adopting these new requirements in
2009 and 2008 was not material to Nicor&#8217;s results of operations or financial
condition.</font></div>

a final settlement with the SEC commissioners on claims of securities law

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor
Gas&#8217; inventory is carried at cost on a LIFO basis.&#160;&#160;Nicor Enerchange&#8217;s
inventory is carried at the lower of weighted-average cost or
market.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Based on
the average cost of gas purchased in December 2009 and 2008, the estimated
replacement cost of Nicor Gas&#8217; inventory at December 31, 2009 and 2008 exceeded
the LIFO cost by $288.5 million and $297.7 million, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2009, Nicor Gas liquidated 8.8 Bcf of its LIFO-based inventory at an average
cost per Mcf of $7.83.&#160;&#160;For gas purchased in 2009, the company&#8217;s
average cost per Mcf was $3.89 lower than the average LIFO liquidation
rate.&#160;&#160;Applying LIFO cost in valuing the liquidation, as opposed to
using the average gas purchase cost, had the effect of increasing the cost of
gas in 2009 by $34.3 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2007, Nicor Gas liquidated 7 Bcf of its LIFO-based inventory at an average cost
per Mcf of $5.81.&#160;&#160;For gas purchased in 2007, the company&#8217;s average
cost per Mcf was $0.93 higher than the average LIFO liquidation
rate.&#160;&#160;Applying LIFO cost in valuing the liquidation, as opposed to
using the average gas purchase cost, had the effect of decreasing the cost of
gas in 2007 by $6.4 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There was
no liquidation of LIFO layers during 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Since the
cost of gas, including inventory costs, is charged to customers without markup,
subject to ICC review, the LIFO liquidation in 2009 and 2007 had no impact on
net income.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor
Enerchange recorded charges of $2.8 million, $8.3 million and $5.0 million in
2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively, resulting from lower of cost or market
valuations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">7.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;SHORT-TERM
AND LONG-TERM DEBT</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In July
2009, Nicor Gas, through a private placement, issued $50 million First Mortgage
Bonds at 4.70 percent, due in 2019.&#160;&#160;In February 2009, the $50 million
5.37 percent First Mortgage Bond series matured and was retired.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August
2008, Nicor Gas, through a private placement, issued $75 million First Mortgage
Bonds at 6.25 percent, due in 2038.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas retired the $75 million
5.875 percent First Mortgage Bond series that became due in August
2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Substantially
all gas distribution properties are subject to the lien of the indenture
securing Nicor Gas&#8217; First Mortgage Bonds.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May
2009, Nicor Gas established a $550 million, 364-day revolver, expiring May 2010,
to replace the $600 million, nine-month seasonal revolver, which expired in May
2009.&#160;&#160;In September 2005, Nicor and Nicor Gas established a $600
million, five-year revolver, expiring September 2010.&#160;&#160;These
facilities were established with major domestic and foreign banks and serve as
backup for the issuance of commercial paper.&#160;&#160;The company had $494.0
million and $739.9 million of commercial paper outstanding with a
weighted-average interest rate of 0.1 percent and 0.4 percent at December 31,
2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
company believes it is in compliance with all debt covenants.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
company incurred total interest expense of $38.8 million, $40.3 million, and
$38.2 million in 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;Interest expense
is reported net of amounts capitalized.&#160;&#160;Interest expense capitalized
for the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007 was $0.1 million, $0.2
million and $0.3 million, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor Gas
may not extend cash advances to an affiliate if Nicor Gas has any outstanding
short-term borrowings.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas&#8217; practice also provides that the
balance of cash deposits or advances from Nicor Gas to an affiliate at any time
shall not exceed the unused balance of funds actually available to that
affiliate under its existing bank credit agreements or its commercial paper
facilities with unaffiliated third parties.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas&#8217; positive cash
deposits, if any, may be applied by Nicor to offset negative balances of other
Nicor subsidiaries and vice versa.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">8.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;FAIR
VALUE MEASUREMENTS</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair
value of assets and liabilities that are measured on a recurring basis are
categorized in the table below (in millions) into three broad levels (with Level
1 considered the most reliable) based upon the valuation inputs.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">When
available and appropriate, the company uses quoted market prices in active
markets to determine fair value and classifies such items within Level
1.&#160;&#160;For derivatives, Level 1 values include only those derivative
instruments traded on the NYMEX.&#160;&#160;The company enters into
over-the-counter instruments with values that are similar to, and correlate
with, quoted prices for exchange-traded instruments in active markets; these
over-the-counter items are classified within Level 2.&#160;&#160;In certain
instances, the company may be required to use one or more significant
unobservable inputs for a model-derived valuation; the resulting valuation is
classified as Level 3.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The net
fair value of derivatives relates largely to Nicor Gas.&#160;&#160;The majority
of derivatives held by Nicor Gas are for the purpose of hedging natural gas
purchases for its customers, and therefore their fair values do not affect net
income, as their settlement is passed directly through to customers without
markup, subject to ICC review.&#160;&#160;The change in fair value for these
derivatives is accounted for through regulatory assets and
liabilities.</font></div>

net derivative asset balances for the periods ended December 31 (in

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor

approximately three years.&#160;&#160;Commodity price-risk exposure arising from
Nicor Enerchange&#8217;s activities and Nicor Gas&#8217; natural gas purchases for company
use is mitigated with derivative instruments that total to a net short position
of 1.3 Bcf as of December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The above volumes exclude

require the company to post collateral if the company&#8217;s net liability position
exceeds a specified threshold.&#160;&#160;Also, certain derivative agreements
contain credit-risk-related contingent features, whereby the company would be
required to provide additional collateral or pay the amount due to the
counterparty when a credit event occurs, such as if the company&#8217;s credit rating
was to be lowered.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, for agreements with such

$20 million, for which the company had posted no collateral to its
counterparties.&#160;&#160;If it was assumed that the </font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
decrease in the liability for unrecognized tax benefits in 2009 when compared to
the prior year is due primarily to the settlement of an item concerning the
timing of inclusion in taxable income of recoveries for environmental clean-up
expenditures, partially offset by other settlements, adjustments and
accruals.&#160;&#160;The increase in the liability for unrecognized tax benefits
in 2008 when compared to the prior year is due primarily to an item concerning
the timing of inclusion in taxable income of recoveries for environmental
clean-up expenditures, partially offset by settlements and adjustments to
estimates.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At
December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007, there were $4.6 million, $2.5 million and $5.7
million, respectively, of unrecognized tax benefits that if recognized, would
affect the company&#8217;s annual effective tax rate.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If
settlements vary from these estimated amounts recognized for unrecognized tax
benefits, the company does not anticipate any adjustment would result in a
material change to its financial position.&#160;&#160;However, the company
believes that it is reasonably possible that a change to its liability for
unrecognized tax benefits could occur within 12 months, potentially increasing
by $2 million or decreasing by $10 million its unrecognized tax
benefit.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
company recognized net interest expense (income) on tax matters of approximately
$1 million, ($3) million and ($6) million in 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.&#160;&#160;In the fourth quarter of 2007, Nicor recorded the
effects of a settlement with the IRS related to the timing of certain deductions
taken as part of a change in accounting method on its 2002 tax
return.&#160;&#160;As a result of the settlement, Nicor reduced its reserve for
interest payable by $9.6 million.&#160;&#160;The company had approximately $5
million of interest receivable at December 31, 2009 compared with $9 million of
interest receivable as of December 31, 2008.&#160;&#160;The change is due
primarily to the settlement of interest in the first quarter of 2009 related to
a state income tax matter.&#160;&#160;Amounts recognized in operating expense
related to penalties were insignificant.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2006,
the company reorganized certain shipping and related operations.&#160;&#160;The
reorganization allows the company to take advantage of certain provisions of the
Jobs Act that provide the opportunity for tax savings subsequent to the date of
the reorganization.&#160;&#160;Generally, to the extent foreign shipping
earnings are not repatriated to the United States, such earnings are not
expected to be subject to current taxation.&#160;&#160;In addition, to the
extent such earnings are expected to be indefinitely reinvested offshore, no
deferred income tax expense would be recorded by the company.&#160;&#160;For the
years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007, income tax expense has not been
provided on approximately $19 million, $23 million and $39 million,
respectively, of foreign company shipping earnings.</font></div>

company&#8217;s postretirement benefit costs have historically been considered in rate
proceedings in the period they are accrued.&#160;&#160;As a regulated utility,
Nicor Gas expects continued rate recovery of the eligible costs of its defined
benefit postretirement plans and, accordingly, associated changes in the plan&#8217;s
funded status have been deferred as a regulatory asset or liability until
recognized in net income, instead of being recorded in accumulated other
comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;However, to the extent Nicor Gas employees
perform services for non-regulated affiliates and to the extent such employees
are eligible to participate in these plans, the affiliates are charged for the
cost of these benefits and the changes in the funded status relating to these
employees are recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income.</font></div>

and 2008 discount rates for each plan were determined by performing a cash flow
matching study using the Citigroup Pension Discount Curve.&#160;&#160;The
Citigroup Pension Discount Curve is constructed from a Treasury yield curve and
adjusted by adding a corporate bond spread.&#160;&#160;The corporate bond spread
is developed from a large pool of high quality corporate bonds and mitigates the
risks associated with selecting individual corporate bonds whose values may not
be representative of the broader market.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003 continues
to provide a prescription drug benefit as well as a potential federal subsidy to
sponsors of certain retiree health care benefit plans whose prescription drug
benefits are actuarially equivalent to the Medicare Part D
benefit.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas has determined that the prescription drug benefits
of its plan are actuarially equivalent and accordingly has reflected the effects
of the subsidy in its determination of the benefit obligation and annual net
benefit cost.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
company&#8217;s investment objective relating to pension plan assets is to provide a
total investment return which will allow the pension plan to meet its remaining
benefit obligations.&#160; The company&#8217;s investment strategy is to diversify its
investments among asset classes in order to reduce risk.&#160;&#160;Investment
performance is measured against a targeted rate of return which reflects the
asset allocation of the plan assets and an appropriate published index return
for each asset class.&#160;&#160;The company will rebalance the investment
portfolio periodically if the actual asset allocation is significantly out of
tolerance from the target allocation.</font></div>

            <td valign="bottom" width="12%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">100%</font></td>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2009,
the company transitioned its target allocation from a 69% equity, 31% fixed
income allocation to the target allocation shown above.&#160;&#160;In addition,
the company adopted a long-duration, primarily corporate bond investment
strategy for the fixed income portion of the plan assets to improve duration
matching between plan assets and benefit obligations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Equity
investments are comprised of certain common collective trusts which invest in
U.S. and international equity securities.&#160;&#160;U.S. equity holdings are
diversified across the small, mid and large cap asset
classes.&#160;&#160;International investments are diversified across countries
and capitalization size in order to maintain a broad market representation of
non-U.S. markets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fixed
income investments are diversified across a broad range of investment grade
corporate bonds and other fixed income securities.&#160;&#160;The fixed income
portfolio is targeted to maintain an average credit quality rating of at least
single-A and a weighted duration that approximates the duration of the expected
benefit obligations.</font></div>

difference between the proceeds from the exercise of stock options and the par
value of the stock is recorded within Paid-in capital on the Consolidated
Statements of Capitalization.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Restricted
stock.</font>&#160;&#160;Restricted stock represents shares of common stock that
generally vest based on continued employment at the end of a four-year
period.&#160;&#160;Vesting can be accelerated due to certain events such as
retirement, change in control, death or disability.&#160;&#160;The fair value of
the restricted stock is determined using the company&#8217;s closing stock price on
the grant date.&#160;&#160;Compensation cost, measured using the grant date fair
value adjusted for a historical forfeiture rate, is recognized over the
requisite service period.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Dividend

restrictions on the payment of dividends.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas is restricted by
regulation in the amount it can dividend or loan to
affiliates.&#160;&#160;Dividends are allowed only to the extent of Nicor Gas&#8217;
retained earnings balance.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">14.&#160;&#160;&#160;MANDATORILY
REDEEMABLE PREFERRED STOCK</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Voting.</font>&#160;&#160;Each share
of preferred stock, regardless of class, entitles the holder to one vote as to
matters considered at the company&#8217;s annual meeting of shareholders.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mandatorily redeemable preferred
stock.&#160;&#160;</font>In 2009 and 2007, Nicor redeemed 10,150 and 100 shares,
respectively, of 4.48 percent Mandatorily Redeemable Preferred Stock, $50 par
value, at an average redemption price of $46.43 and $43.00 per share,
respectively, plus accrued unpaid dividends.&#160;&#160;There were 1,431 shares
of the 4.48 percent Series Mandatorily Redeemable Preferred Stock, $50 par
value, outstanding at December 31, 2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">15.&#160;&#160;&#160;BUSINESS
SEGMENT AND GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor is
a holding company that operates in three separately managed reportable business
segments: gas distribution, shipping and wholesale marketing.&#160;&#160;The gas
distribution segment, Nicor&#8217;s principal business, serves 2.2 million customers
in a service territory that encompasses most of the northern third of Illinois,
excluding the city of Chicago.&#160;&#160;The shipping segment transports
containerized freight between Florida, the eastern coast of Canada, the Bahamas
and the Caribbean region.&#160;&#160;The shipping segment also includes amounts
related to cargo insurance coverage sold to its customers and other third
parties.&#160;&#160;The wholesale marketing segment engages in wholesale
marketing of natural gas supply services primarily in the Midwest, administers
the Chicago Hub for Nicor Gas, serves commercial and industrial customers in the
Chicago market area, and manages Nicor Solutions&#8217; and Nicor Advanced Energy&#8217;s
product risks, including the purchases of natural gas supplies.</font></div>

revenues include gas distribution revenues related to customers entering into
utility-bill management contracts with Nicor Solutions and wholesale marketing
revenues from the sale of natural gas to Nicor Advanced Energy.&#160;&#160;Under
the utility-bill management contracts, Nicor Solutions bills a fixed amount to a
customer, regardless of changes in natural gas prices or weather, and in
exchange pays the customer&#8217;s utility bills from Nicor Gas.&#160;&#160;Nicor
Advanced Energy provides natural gas and related services on an unregulated
basis to residential and small commercial customers and purchases most of its
natural gas supplies from Nicor Enerchange.&#160;&#160;Intersegment revenues are
eliminated in the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

obligations consist of a natural gas transportation agreement and property,
plant and equipment purchases.&#160;&#160;Operating leases are primarily for
vessels, containers and equipment in the shipping business, office space and
equipment in the gas distribution business and office space for the company&#8217;s
other energy ventures.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Tropical
Shipping has certain equipment operating leases which include purchase and/or
renewal options, at fair market amounts at the time of purchase or
renewal.&#160;&#160;Rental expense under operating leases was $31.4 million,
$41.7 million and $41.3 million in 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">19.&#160;&#160;&#160;REGULATORY
PROCEEDINGS</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Rate proceeding.&#160;&#160;</font>On
March 25, 2009, the ICC issued an order approving an increase in base revenues
of approximately $69 million, a rate of return on rate base of 7.58 percent and
a rate of return on equity of 10.17 percent.&#160;&#160;The order also approved
an energy efficiency rider.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas placed the rates approved in
the March 25, 2009 order into effect on April 3, 2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: -9pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On April
24, 2009, Nicor Gas filed a request for rehearing with the ICC concerning the
capital structure and return on equity contained in the ICC&#8217;s rate order
contending the company&#8217;s return on rate base should be higher.&#160;&#160;On May
13, 2009, the ICC agreed to conduct a rehearing concerning the capital structure
but denied the remainder of the company&#8217;s request.&#160;&#160;On October 7,
2009, the ICC issued its decision on rehearing in which it increased the annual
base revenues approved for Nicor Gas in the March 25, 2009 order by
approximately $11 million, increasing the rate of return on rate base to 8.09
percent.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas placed the rates approved in the rehearing
decision into effect on a prospective basis on October 15,
2009.&#160;&#160;Therefore, the total annual base revenue increase resulting
from the rate case originally filed by the company in April 2008 is
approximately $80 million.&#160;&#160;In December 2009, Nicor Gas withdrew
appeals of the ICC rate orders that it previously had filed in state appellate
court.&#160;&#160;The ICC&#8217;s decision on rehearing, therefore, is final and no
longer subject to appeal.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Bad debt rider.</font>&#160;&#160;In
September 2009, Nicor Gas filed for approval of a bad debt rider with the ICC
under an Illinois state law which took effect in July 2009.&#160;&#160;On
February 2, 2010, the ICC issued an order approving the company&#8217;s proposed bad
debt rider.&#160;&#160;This rider will provide for recovery from customers of
the amount over the benchmark for bad debt expense established in the company&#8217;s
rate cases.&#160;&#160;It will also provide for refunds to customers if bad debt
expense is below such benchmarks.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As a
result of the February order, Nicor Gas will record in the first quarter of 2010
a net recovery related to 2008 and 2009 of approximately $32 million;
substantially all of this amount is expected to be collected in
2010.&#160;&#160;The benchmark, against which 2010 actual bad debt expense will
be compared, is approximately $63 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">20.&#160;&#160;&#160;GUARANTEES
AND INDEMNITIES</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor and
certain subsidiaries enter into various financial and performance guarantees and
indemnities providing assurance to third parties.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financial
guarantees.&#160;&#160;</font>TEL has an obligation to restore to zero any
deficit in its equity account for income tax purposes in the unlikely event that
Triton is liquidated and a deficit balance remains.&#160;&#160;This obligation
continues for the life of the Triton partnerships and any payment is effectively
limited to the assets of TEL, which were approximately $5 million at December
31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Nicor believes the likelihood of any such payment by TEL is
remote.&#160;&#160;No liability has been recorded for this
obligation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Performance guarantees. </font>Nicor
Services markets product warranty contracts that provide for the repair of
heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment, natural gas lines and other
appliances within homes.&#160;&#160;Revenues from these product warranty
contracts are recognized ratably over the coverage period, and related repair
costs are charged to expense as incurred.&#160;&#160;Repair expenses of $7.9
million, $7.1 million and $6.6 million were incurred in 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>

    <div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Indemnities.</font>&#160;&#160;In
certain instances, Nicor has undertaken to indemnify current property owners and
others against costs associated with the effects and/or remediation of
contaminated sites for which the company may be responsible under applicable
federal or state environmental laws, generally with no limitation as to the
amount.&#160;&#160;These indemnifications relate primarily to ongoing coal tar
cleanup, as discussed in Note 21 &#8211; Contingencies &#8211; Manufactured Gas Plant
Sites.&#160;&#160;Nicor believes that the likelihood of payment under its other
environmental indemnifications is remote.&#160;&#160;No liability has been
recorded for such indemnifications.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor has
also indemnified, to the fullest extent permitted under the laws of the State of
Illinois and any other applicable laws, its present and former directors,
officers and employees against expenses they may incur in connection with
litigation they are a party to by reason of their association with the
company.&#160;&#160;There is generally no limitation as to the amount.&#160;
During 2007, the SEC filed a civil injunctive action against three former
officers of Nicor relating to the PBR plan.&#160;&#160;Defense costs that are
being incurred by these former officers in connection with the SEC action
currently are being tendered to, and paid by, the company&#8217;s
insurer.&#160;&#160;While the company does not expect to incur significant costs
relating to the indemnification of present and former directors, officers and
employees after taking into account available insurance, it is not possible to
estimate the maximum future potential payments.</font></div>

            <td width="955">
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CONTINGENCIES</font></font></div>
