    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following contingencies of Nicor are in various stages of investigation or
disposition.&#160;&#160;Although in some cases the company is unable to estimate
the amount of loss reasonably possible in addition to any amounts already
recognized, it is possible that the resolution of these contingencies, either
individually or in aggregate, will require the company to take charges against,
or will result in reductions in, future earnings.&#160;&#160;It is the opinion
of management that the resolution of these contingencies, either individually or
in aggregate, could be material to earnings in a particular period but is not
expected to have a material adverse impact on Nicor&#8217;s liquidity or financial
condition.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">PBR Plan.&#160;&#160;</font>Nicor
Gas&#8217; PBR plan for natural gas costs went into effect in 2000 and was terminated
by the company effective January 1, 2003.&#160;&#160;Under the PBR plan, Nicor
Gas&#8217; total gas supply costs were compared to a market-sensitive
benchmark.&#160;&#160;Savings and losses relative to the benchmark were
determined annually and shared equally with sales customers.&#160;&#160;The PBR
plan is currently under ICC review.&#160;&#160;There are allegations that the
company acted improperly in connection with the PBR plan, and the ICC and others
are reviewing these allegations.&#160;&#160;On June 27, 2002, the Citizens
Utility Board (&#8220;CUB&#8221;) filed a motion to reopen the record in the ICC&#8217;s
proceedings to review the PBR plan (the &#8220;ICC Proceedings&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As a
result of the motion to reopen, Nicor Gas, the staff of the ICC and CUB entered
into a stipulation providing for additional discovery.&#160;&#160;The Illinois
Attorney General&#8217;s Office (&#8220;IAGO&#8221;) has also intervened in this
matter.&#160;&#160;In addition, the IAGO issued Civil Investigation Demands
(&#8220;CIDs&#8221;) to CUB and the ICC staff.&#160;&#160;The CIDs ordered that CUB and the
ICC staff produce all documents relating to any claims that Nicor Gas may have
presented, or caused to be presented, false information related to its PBR
plan.&#160;&#160;The company has committed to cooperate fully in the reviews of
the PBR plan.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
response to these allegations, on July 18, 2002, the Nicor Board of Directors
appointed a special committee of independent, non-management directors to
conduct an inquiry into issues surrounding natural gas purchases, sales,
transportation, storage and such other matters as may come to the attention of
the special committee in the course of its investigation.&#160;&#160;The special
committee presented the report of its counsel (&#8220;Report&#8221;) to Nicor&#8217;s Board of
Directors on October 28, 2002.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
response, the Nicor Board of Directors directed the company&#8217;s management to,
among other things, make appropriate adjustments to account for, and fully
address, the adverse consequences to ratepayers of the items noted in the
Report, and conduct a detailed study of the adequacy of internal accounting and
regulatory controls.&#160;&#160;The adjustments were made in prior years&#8217;
financial statements resulting in a $24.8 million liability.&#160;&#160;Included
in such $24.8 million liability is a $4.1 million loss contingency.&#160;&#160;A
$1.8</font></div>

    <div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">million
adjustment to the previously recorded liability, which is discussed below, was
made in 2004 increasing the recorded liability to $26.6
million.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas estimates that there is $26.9 million due to the
company from the 2002 PBR plan year, which has not been recognized in the
financial statements due to uncertainties surrounding the PBR
plan.&#160;&#160;In addition, interest due to the company on certain components
of these amounts has not been recognized in the financial statements due to the
same uncertainties.&#160;&#160;By the end of 2003, the company completed steps
to correct the weaknesses and deficiencies identified in the detailed study of
the adequacy of internal controls.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Pursuant
to the agreement of all parties, including the company, the ICC re-opened the
1999 and 2000 purchased gas adjustment filings for review of certain
transactions related to the PBR plan and consolidated the reviews of the
1999-2002 purchased gas adjustment filings with the PBR plan
review.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
February 5, 2003, CUB filed a motion for $27 million in sanctions against the
company in the ICC Proceedings.&#160;&#160;In that motion, CUB alleged that
Nicor Gas&#8217; responses to certain CUB data requests were false.&#160;&#160;Also on
February 5, 2003, CUB stated in a press release that, in addition to $27 million
in sanctions, it would seek additional refunds to consumers.&#160;&#160;On March
5, 2003, the ICC staff filed a response brief in support of CUB&#8217;s motion for
sanctions.&#160;&#160;On May 1, 2003, the ALJs assigned to the proceeding issued
a ruling denying CUB&#8217;s motion for sanctions.&#160;&#160;CUB has filed an appeal
of the motion for sanctions with the ICC, and the ICC has indicated that it will
not rule on the appeal until the final disposition of the ICC
Proceedings.&#160;&#160;It is not possible to determine how the ICC will resolve
the claims of CUB or other parties to the ICC Proceedings.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2004,
the company became aware of additional information relating to the activities of
individuals affecting the PBR plan for the period from 1999 through 2002,
including information consisting of third party documents and recordings of
telephone conversations from Entergy-Koch Trading, LP (&#8220;EKT&#8221;), a natural gas,
storage and transportation trader and consultant with whom Nicor did business
under the PBR plan.&#160;&#160;Review of additional information completed in
2004 resulted in the $1.8 million adjustment to the previously recorded
liability referenced above.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
evidentiary hearings on this matter were stayed in 2004 in order to permit the
parties to undertake additional third party discovery from EKT.&#160;&#160;In
December 2006, the additional third party discovery from EKT was obtained and
the ALJs issued a scheduling order that provided for Nicor Gas to submit direct
testimony by April 13, 2007.&#160;&#160;In its direct testimony, Nicor Gas seeks
a reimbursement of approximately $6 million, which includes interest due to the
company, as noted above, of $1.6 million, as of March 31, 2007.&#160;&#160;In
September 2009, the staff of the ICC, IAGO and CUB submitted direct testimony to
the ICC requesting refunds of $109 million, $255 million and $286 million,
respectively.&#160;&#160;No date has been set for evidentiary hearings on this
matter.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor is
unable to predict the outcome of the ICC&#8217;s review or the company&#8217;s potential
exposure thereunder.&#160;&#160;Because the PBR plan and historical gas costs
are still under ICC review, the final outcome could be materially different than
the amounts reflected in the company&#8217;s financial statements as of December 31,
2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mercury.</font>&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas
has incurred, and expects to continue to incur, costs related to its historical
use of mercury in various kinds of company equipment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of
December 31, 2009, Nicor Gas had remaining an estimated liability of $2.1
million related to inspection, cleanup and legal defense costs.&#160;&#160;This
represents management&#8217;s best estimate of future costs based on an evaluation of
currently available information.&#160;&#160;Actual costs may vary from this
estimate.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas remains a defendant in several private lawsuits,
all in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, seeking a variety of
unquantified damages (including bodily injury and property damages)

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">allegedly
caused by mercury spillage resulting from the removal of mercury-containing
regulators.&#160;&#160;Potential liabilities relating to these claims have been
assumed by a contractor&#8217;s insurer subject to certain limitations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The final
disposition of these mercury-related matters is not expected to have a material
adverse impact on the company&#8217;s liquidity or financial condition.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Manufactured Gas Plant
Sites.</font>&#160;&#160;Manufactured gas plants were used in the 1800&#8217;s and
early to mid 1900&#8217;s to produce manufactured gas from coal, creating a coal tar
byproduct.&#160;&#160;Current environmental laws may require the cleanup of coal
tar at certain former manufactured gas plant sites.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Nicor Gas
has identified properties for which it may have some
responsibility.&#160;&#160;Most of these properties are not presently owned by
the company.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas and Commonwealth Edison Company (&#8220;ComEd&#8221;) are
parties to an agreement to cooperate in cleaning up residue at many of these
properties.&#160;&#160;The agreement allocates to Nicor Gas 51.73 percent of
cleanup costs for 24 sites, no portion of the cleanup costs for 14 other sites
and 50 percent of general remediation program costs that do not relate
exclusively to particular sites.&#160;&#160;Information regarding preliminary
site reviews has been presented to the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency
for certain properties.&#160;&#160;More detailed investigations and remedial
activities are complete, in progress or planned at many of these
sites.&#160;&#160;The results of the detailed site-by-site investigations will
determine the extent additional remediation is necessary and provide a basis for
estimating additional future costs.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, the
company had recorded a liability in connection with these matters of $23.8
million.&#160;&#160;In accordance with ICC authorization, the company has been
recovering, and expects to continue to recover, these costs from its customers,
subject to annual prudence reviews.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In April
2002, Nicor Gas was named as a defendant, together with ComEd, in a lawsuit
brought by the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago (the
&#8220;MWRDGC&#8221;) under the Federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation
and Liability Act seeking recovery of past and future remediation costs and a
declaration of the level of appropriate cleanup for a former manufactured gas
plant site in Skokie, Illinois now owned by the MWRDGC.&#160;&#160;In January
2003, the suit was amended to include a claim under the Federal Resource
Conservation and Recovery Act.&#160;&#160;The suit was filed in the United
States District Court for the Northern District of
Illinois.&#160;&#160;Management cannot predict the outcome of this litigation or
the company&#8217;s potential exposure thereto, if any, and has not recorded a
liability associated with this contingency.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Since
costs and recoveries relating to the cleanup of manufactured gas plant sites are
passed directly through to customers in accordance with ICC regulations, subject
to an annual ICC prudence review, the final disposition of manufactured gas
plant matters is not expected to have a material impact on the company&#8217;s
financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Municipal Tax
Matters.</font>&#160;&#160;Many municipalities in Nicor Gas&#8217; service territory
have enacted ordinances that impose taxes on gas sales to customers within
municipal boundaries.&#160;&#160;Most of these municipal taxes are imposed on
Nicor Gas based on revenues generated by Nicor Gas within the
municipality.&#160;&#160;Other municipal taxes are imposed on natural gas
consumers within the municipality but are collected from consumers and remitted
to the municipality by Nicor Gas.&#160;&#160;A number of municipalities have
instituted audits of Nicor Gas&#8217; tax remittances.&#160;&#160;In May 2007, five of
those municipalities filed an action against Nicor Gas in state court in DuPage
County, Illinois relating to these tax audits.&#160;&#160;Following a dismissal
of this action without prejudice by the trial court, the municipalities filed an
amended complaint.&#160;&#160;The amended complaint seeks, among other things,
compensation for alleged unpaid taxes.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas is contesting the
claims in the amended complaint.&#160;&#160;In December 2007, 25 additional
municipalities, all represented by the same audit firm involved in the lawsuit,
issued assessments to Nicor Gas claiming that it failed to provide information
requested by the audit firm and owed the municipalities back
taxes.&#160;&#160;Nicor Gas believes the assessments are improper and has
challenged them.&#160;&#160;While the company is unable to predict the outcome
of these matters or to reasonably estimate its potential exposure related
thereto, if </font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Controls and

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Evaluation
of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
company carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the
participation of the company&#8217;s management, including its Chief Executive Officer
and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of
the company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the most
recent fiscal quarter of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K
(the &#8220;Evaluation&#8221;).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, management
recognizes that any disclosure controls and procedures, no matter how well
designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the
desired control objectives, and management is required to apply its judgment in
evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible disclosure controls and
procedures.&#160;&#160;These disclosure controls and procedures are designed so
that required information is accumulated and communicated to the registrant&#8217;s
management, including its principal executive officer and principal financial
officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required
disclosures.&#160;&#160;Based on the Evaluation, the company&#8217;s Chief Executive
Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that the company&#8217;s disclosure
controls and procedures, as of the end of the most recent fiscal quarter covered
by this Annual Report on Form 10-K, were effective at the reasonable assurance
level to ensure that information required to be disclosed by the company in
reports that it files or submits under the Securities </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Exchange
Act of 1934 is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time
periods specified in United States Securities and Exchange Commission rules and
forms.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Management&#8217;s
Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Internal
control over financial reporting refers to the process designed by, or under the
supervision of, the company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial
Officer, and effected by the company&#8217;s board of directors, management and other
personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of
financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external
purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and
includes those policies and procedures that:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div>
      <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
              <div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">1.&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Pertain
      to the maintenance of records that in reasonable detail accurately and
      fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the
      company;</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div>
      <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
              <div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2.&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Provide
      reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit
      preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted
      accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company
      are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and
      directors of the company; and</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>

<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
              <div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">3.&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Provide
      reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of
      unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that
      could have a material effect on the financial
  statements.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>

        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents </a></font></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div>&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Internal
control over financial reporting cannot provide absolute assurance of achieving
financial reporting objectives because of its inherent
limitations.&#160;&#160;Internal control over financial reporting is a process
that involves human diligence and compliance and is subject to lapses in
judgment and breakdowns resulting from human failures.&#160;&#160;Internal
control over financial reporting also can be circumvented by collusion or
improper management override.&#160;&#160;Because of such limitations, there is a
risk that material misstatements may not be prevented or detected on a timely
basis by internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;However, these
inherent limitations are known features of the financial reporting
process.&#160;&#160;Therefore, it is possible to design into the process
safeguards to reduce, though not eliminate, this risk.&#160;&#160;Management is
responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over
financial reporting for the company.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Management
has used the framework set forth in the report entitled &#8220;Internal
Control&#8212;Integrated Framework&#8221; published by the Committee of Sponsoring
Organizations of the Treadway Commission to evaluate the effectiveness of the
company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;Management has
concluded that the company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting was
effective as of December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Deloitte &amp; Touche LLP, an
independent registered public accounting firm, has issued an attestation report
on&#160;the company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There has
been no change in the company&#8217;s internal controls over financial reporting
during the company&#8217;s most recent fiscal quarter that has materially affected, or
is reasonably likely to materially affect, the company&#8217;s internal control over
financial reporting.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.5"><br></div>
